clue.text: Weigh up defence's case and set free

indicators.note: a case is the outside of something, so the outer letters of the word defence are taken

parts.note: to set free is to liberate

explanation.surface: A judge weighs the defence's argument before releasing the accused.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Case' looks like a legal case, but it means the outside: DE, the first and last letters of 'defence'.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to weigh up a matter is to consider it carefully.

clue.text: Share identification in club with a poor reputation

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation inside the word for the seedy club

parts.note: a dive is a seedy bar or nightclub

explanation.surface: Someone shows their ID to get into a disreputable nightclub.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to share something out is to split it among people.

clue.text: People who fail in ambitious resolutions turning up

indicators.note: turning up says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Those who make over-ambitious New Year resolutions tend to fail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' leads to the run SRESOL inside 'ambitious resolutions'; 'turning up' in a down clue reads it from the bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: those who fail at something are the ones who lose.

clue.text: Getting on train for Harrow, perhaps

parts.note: boarding a vehicle is getting on it
to school is to train or teach

explanation.surface: A traveller boarding a train for Harrow, a district of north-west London.
explanation.walkthrough: Harrow is also a famous English private school where pupils live in.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: Harrow is a well-known residential private school, hence the 'perhaps'.

clue.text: Doctor from Bognor perhaps starts to treat rheum after rhinoplasty

parts.note: Bognor Regis is a seaside town, one of several places whose name ends in Regis

indicators.note: starts to means the opening letter of each following word is taken

explanation.surface: A doctor from a seaside town treats a runny nose after a nose job.
explanation.walkthrough: Bognor Regis is an English seaside resort; Lyme Regis is another, hence 'perhaps'.
explanation.definitionFit: In British hospitals a registrar is a grade of doctor below consultant.

clue.text: Cosmetic surgery to tensor with no end of problems

indicators.note: surgery reshapes something, so the remaining letters are rearranged
with no says a letter is removed from the word tensor
end of picks the final letter of the word problems

explanation.surface: Cosmetic surgery on a tensor muscle that leaves no problems.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with no end of problems' takes S from TENSOR, leaving TENOR; 'surgery' rearranges those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a toner is a skin lotion, one of many cosmetics.

clue.text: Measure that's too expensive to lose heart

indicators.note: to lose heart means the central letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: a steep price is too high

explanation.surface: A shopper's precaution: a measure to avoid losing heart at high prices.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a step is a measure taken to achieve something.

clue.text: Shows nervousness seeing the Yorkshire charmers

parts.note: in Yorkshire dialect 'the' is clipped to t'
witches cast charms, so they are charmers

explanation.surface: Someone gets jittery when watching Yorkshire snake charmers or enchantresses.
explanation.walkthrough: Yorkshire speech famously shortens 'the' to t'.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a person who twitches is making small nervous jerks.

clue.text: Signs left on board sent off

parts.note: port is the left side aboard a ship

indicators.note: off means the letters of sent are disordered

explanation.surface: A sailor on the left side of the deck has been sent off.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: portents are omens or signs of things to come.

clue.text: Big city's argument against Mediterranean island forest

parts.note: the cons are the arguments against, as in pros and cons
Crete is a large Greek island in the Mediterranean
a jungle is a dense tropical forest

explanation.surface: A city's debate over a forest on a Mediterranean island.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: a concrete jungle is a big, harsh urban sprawl.

clue.text: Sight victory as it evolves

parts.note: V is short for victory, as in V-sign

indicators.note: evolves means the letters of as it change shape

explanation.surface: Watching victory take shape as the situation develops.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a vista is a view, something seen.

clue.text: Person doomed to carry fallen idol is canal worker

indicators.note: to carry means one word holds the other inside it

parts.note: a goner is someone beyond saving

indicators.note: fallen means the letters of idol tumble into a new order

explanation.surface: A doomed man hauling a toppled statue turns out to work on a canal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fallen' reads as part of the story but signals the anagram (DOLI); 'to carry' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A gondolier rows a gondola, typically on the canals of Venice.

clue.text: Makes fun of date disheartened with fairground attractions

indicators.note: disheartened means the middle letters of date are removed

parts.note: rides such as the big wheel are fairground attractions

explanation.surface: A date ends badly at the fair, with mockery on the rides.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: someone who derides another mocks or ridicules them.

clue.text: Revolution by engineers to be green

parts.note: RE stands for the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps
a cycle is one revolution or turn

explanation.surface: An engineers' revolution with an environmental goal.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: being green means acting in an eco-friendly way, such as reprocessing waste.

clue.text: Offence of men renting if thrown out

indicators.note: thrown out means the letters are scattered and reassembled

explanation.surface: Tenants evicted for an offence against their lease.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an infringement is a violation of a rule, an offence.

clue.text: Fruit that may be source of honey in Spain

parts.note: bees make honey from nectar
E is the international vehicle code for Spain (España)

explanation.surface: Wondering whether a Spanish fruit could be a honey source.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that may be' is a link phrase; bees gather nectar to make honey.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a nectarine is a smooth-skinned variety of peach.

clue.text: Food outlet folds before spring

parts.note: tucks are folds sewn in fabric
a hop is a small spring or jump

explanation.surface: A food stall closes up shop ahead of spring.
explanation.walkthrough: A tuck shop is a British school snack shop, 'tuck' being slang for sweets and snacks.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a tuck shop is a small outlet selling food at a school.

clue.text: Weather feature that is on river edge

parts.note: a front is a boundary between air masses on a weather map
i.e. abbreviates id est, that is

explanation.surface: A weather front moving along a river's edge.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a frontier is a border, the edge of a territory.

clue.text: Eastern firm employed by a French communist is open to all

parts.note: un is the French for a

indicators.note: employed by puts the following letters inside the word for a leftist

parts.note: a red is a communist
strict means firm or rigid

explanation.surface: An Eastern company hires a French communist and is open to everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Employed by' is the container signal: the Eastern firm goes inside the communist, not the other way round.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something without restrictions is available to anyone.

clue.text: Poems on South American port

parts.note: odes are lyric poems
SA abbreviates South America

explanation.surface: Poems about a South American port town.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: Odessa is a major Black Sea port in Ukraine.

clue.text: Furrow, seeing circle in wood

indicators.note: in places the ring shape inside the word for a small wood

parts.note: a grove is a small wood
O is shaped like a circle

explanation.surface: Ploughing a furrow and seeing a fairy ring in the wood.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a groove is a long narrow channel, as is a furrow.

clue.text: Office of monarch ignoring government's fellow feeling

indicators.note: ignoring says a letter is left out of the word for royal office

parts.note: kingship is the office or rank of a king

explanation.surface: A monarch who ignores the government's sense of fellowship.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: kinship can mean sympathy or affinity between people.

clue.text: Unhappy Londoner holding post carrying power

indicators.note: holding means the answer sits inside the clue words

explanation.surface: A disgruntled Londoner keeps his job carrying the city's power supply.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unhappy' looks like an anagram signal, but the letters are inside 'unhapPY LONdoner'.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: a pylon is a tall tower supporting electricity cables.

clue.text: European articles will come after a second apart

indicators.note: will come after puts the European words behind the short time unit

parts.note: un is a French article and der a German one

explanation.surface: European articles arrive a second apart.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: torn asunder means split apart.

clue.text: The people's vote in Ohio worried head of industry

indicators.note: in places the vote inside the rearranged state name
worried means the letters of Ohio are agitated into a new order

parts.note: a poll is a vote

indicators.note: head of takes the opening letter of industry

explanation.surface: Voting in Ohio disturbs the boss of industry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Worried' signals the anagram of the state (HOIO), and 'in' sets the vote inside it; 'head of' supplies the final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Hoi polloi is Greek for the many, used to mean the common people.

clue.text: Something that blows over, giving great enjoyment

parts.note: a gust is a blast of wind
O is the cricket scoring abbreviation for an over

explanation.surface: A storm that blows over, leaving people relieved and happy.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to do something with gusto is to relish it.

clue.text: Separate skill required after parking

indicators.note: required after puts the word for skill behind the parking symbol

parts.note: P is the road-sign symbol for parking
art is skill, as in the art of conversation

explanation.surface: Separate parking takes some skill.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to part is to divide or separate.

clue.text: Angry about rescheduled event being confirmed

indicators.note: about means the word for angry goes round the other letters

parts.note: irate means angry

indicators.note: rescheduled means the letters of event are reordered

explanation.surface: Someone furious that a confirmed event was rescheduled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rescheduled' signals the anagram (NVETE) and 'about' wraps the angry word round it; 'confirmed' means habitual, not verified.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a confirmed habit, like an inveterate one, is long-established.
